title: Maximum drug-likeness deep learning ensemble prioritizes an antibacterial lead compound
summary: A fivefold maximum drug-likeness strategy using an ensemble of 33 deep learning sub-models prioritized 15 molecules from a 16-million-molecule library. The lead compound M2 showed antibacterial activity with a minimum inhibitory concentration of 25.6 ug/mL, and computed MM-PBSA binding energy of -38.54 kcal/mol and RMSD of 2.8 A compared with cefuroxime. Potency is weak, the binding comparison is computational, and the abstract omits how many of the 15 were active; this is a version 1 preprint.
ai_technology: Ensemble of 33 deep learning sub-models building a 33-dimensional property spectrum to score drug-likeness for virtual screening

evidence.tested: Experimental MIC assay of the lead compound, with MM-PBSA and molecular dynamics computations.
evidence.unknown: Tested organism, activity of the other prioritized molecules and controls; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Ranks library molecules by similarity to approved-drug properties to select candidates.

source_review.scope: Version 1 abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations not retrieved. Full text not accessed. Author affiliations from OpenAlex metadata.
